title: Adjudicating the Safety Case
summary: Work through Adjudicating the Safety Case.

sections: Worked restricted service with stipulated evidence

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Adjudicating the Safety Case** in *Deployment Release* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Deployment Release, § Adjudicating the Safety Case
blocks.md: An algebraically exact stopping equation or contact-force bound still fails to protect a machine if the physical premise beneath its warrant has never been measured on hardware. Adjudicating a safety release case requires checking each warrant against the qualified measurements, justified analysis, or validated operating restrictions that support it. For the warehouse mobile manipulator, the adjudicator takes each of the six claims of a later section in turn, names the physical premise under its warrant, and grades the evidence behind that premise.

questions.q: The section **Adjudicating the Safety Case** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: The release manifest binds every upstream record, the argument digest, binary hashes, calibration, standing conditions, wear budget, expiry, and the adjudicator's signature to one configuration and gates motion fail-closed.

Release adjudicates physical inequalities (stop inside the clear distance, contact force under the assessed limit, WCET inside its deadline) through a claim-argument-evidence case whose warrants say why each piece of evidence supports its claim.

An update reopens the claims whose evidence it touches, an unchanged enforcer binary does not imply an unchanged containment argument, and shadow mode filters candidates while contained canaries qualify them.
Fleet exposure narrows intervals for common outcomes but leaves rare severe outcomes wide, so each outcome's claim is licensed separately and disclosed.
